title.narrative: Lifesaving health and shelter/NFI response to displacement and famine in Habila and Dilling, South Kordofan.

description.narrative: ltpgtHumanitarian needs in South Kordofan, particularly in the localities of Dilling and Habila, are critically high due to ongoing conflict and limited access to humanitarian aid. Vulnerable children and families face barriers to accessing healthcare, shelter and basic services due to the disruption of supplies, infrastructure damages, displacements, and imposed restrictions. Against this backdrop, Save the Children, in partnership with Skills for Nuba Mountain, proposes a twelve-month project that aims to reduce morbidity and mortality and to improve the living conditions and safety of displaced individuals and host communities in Dilling and Habila through a wide range of health and shelter/NFI services. In line with the HRP and cluster objectives, the project will deliver safe, timely, principled and gender-responsive assistance to 20,748nbsppeople and target the most vulnerable population groups such as women, men, children and persons with disabilities. ltbrgtltspangtUnder the Health component, the project aims to reach 14,700 people and provide essential health services, including routine vaccination, through four fixed clinics offering integrated health services, including sexual and reproductive health and nutrition. The project will further enhance health coverage by operationalizing four Primary Health Care Centres facilities and providing risk communication and community engagement. Maternal health services provided will include support for emergency obstetric and newborn care services, essential laboratory support, antenatal care, postnatal care, and awareness sessions on antenatal care at the referral hospital. This integrated project will improve early detection and prevention of communicable diseases and related effects such as malnutrition. With well-integrated patient safety protocols, accessibility, and accountability mechanisms, essential medicines and health supplies, including personal protective equipment, will be provided for target health facilities and mobile teams. SC will also support the delivery of critical routine immunization services. To ensure disease and outbreak prevention, SC will actively support community engagement and health education, including integrated hygiene messages, to all community members regardless of gender, age, or disability, in an inclusive manner.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtUnder the Shelter/NFI component, the project will provide NFI and shelter to support essential daily activities and offer adaptable shelter solutions to 6,048 people in Habila. To this end, SC and the local partner will distribute life-saving in-kind non-food items to the most vulnerable IDPs and host communities, distribute cash for shelter/NFIs to assist affected households to establish or rehabilitate shelters, supply and construct emergency shelter with high-standards and provide materials for the construction of emergency shelter.nbsplt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtSC will leverage its experience and lessons learned from the ongoing SHF intervention in selected localities to provide an effective and inclusive programme and reach the most in need.nbsp The project will address gender issues by collecting and analysing gender and age-disaggregated data to identify gaps, provide gender-sensitive interventions, and ensure women's participation. The project will directly target people with disabilities to ensure their access to services, measured at all stages through the collection of disability-disaggregated data. Risk mitigation measures will be employed at service delivery points to minimize harm to target beneficiaries while accessing services. Do no harm principles will be integral throughout the project lifecycle, spanning from needs assessment and scoping to design, inception, implementation, and monitoring and evaluation.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgt
